zaragoza_bunny_depth_error.description: Depth MAE for the Zaragoza Stanford bunny Fig. 5 target. The paper reports that Quasi-Fresnel achieves the lowest bunny depth error among the compared direct methods. This gym scores the same target on a tracked synthetic Zaragoza-style bunny proxy because the public HDF5 measurements packaged here do not include 2D albedo/depth ground truth.

depth_mae_cm.description: Centimeter-scale depth mean absolute error on the synthetic Zaragoza-style bunny proxy, the headline reconstruction-quality target.

albedo_psnr_db.description: Albedo PSNR on the same synthetic bunny proxy, included to catch methods that preserve depth while degrading reconstructed appearance.

albedo_ssim.description: Albedo SSIM on the same synthetic bunny proxy, a structural image-quality check complementary to depth MAE.

albedo_mae.description: Albedo MAE on the same synthetic bunny proxy, measuring absolute intensity error that neither PSNR nor SSIM alone captures.

zaragoza_efficiency_public_bunny.description: Public Zaragoza efficiency claim from the Results section. The current gym scores machine-independent memory and scaling proxies for the FDH-style aggregated Quasi-Fresnel path on the available public bunny HDF5 measurements, preferring the 64x64 public copy for repeatable CPU jobs.

memory_mb.description: Algorithm peak working memory in megabytes for the low-memory public bunny reconstruction path.

traditional_memory_order.description: Empirical log-log memory scaling slope for the direct reconstruction path, checking that methods do not hide volumetric memory growth outside the primary low-memory path.

loading_memory_order.description: Empirical log-log memory scaling slope for the sequential-loading variant, checking the paper's low-memory complexity claim.

loading_depth_consistency_cm.description: Depth disagreement between the sequential-loading and direct reconstruction paths on the public bunny scene, catching methods whose memory-saving path changes the result.
